mainTopic: The special value of living, dying and being buried in ארץ ישראל (and בבל), including the three oaths and תחיית המתים outside the Land.
overview: The amud opens with the argument between רב יהודה, who forbids leaving בבל for ארץ ישראל, and רבי זירא, who wants to go up. Each time רב יהודה brings a פסוק, רבי זירא shows it is needed for something else, ending with the famous three oaths of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא and the six oaths of רבי לוי. The גמרא then gathers many praises of ארץ ישראל: living there brings forgiveness, burial there is like burial under the מזבח, and leaving it is treated very seriously. It adds a parallel ladder for בבל: leaving בבל for other lands is also forbidden, and living in בבל is like living in ארץ ישראל. Next, רבי אלעזר teaches that only the dead of ארץ ישראל will come back to life. רבי אבא בר ממל challenges him, and the גמרא explains that the righteous outside the Land reach it through tunnels, which is why יעקב and יוסף still wanted burial there. The amud ends with a letter from רבה's brothers urging him to come up and learn from רבי יוחנן, plus health advice in case he stays, and that last discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב יהודה's verse: they will stay in בבל until God recalls them
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק from ירמיהו that רב יהודה uses to forbid leaving בבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: "They shall be taken to Babylonia, and there they shall be until the day I remember them, says ה׳."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the פסוק that is רב יהודה's source. He reads it as saying that the Jews must stay in בבל until ה׳ Himself takes them out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words "and there they shall be until the day I remember them" sound like a command: stay put until ה׳ acts. So, for רב יהודה, a person who leaves בבל on his own is going against this פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: My remembering them, when I take them back

steps.whyThisMatters: Every later step in this section is either an attack on this source or a defense of רב יהודה's position.

phrases.english: "They shall be brought to Babylonia, and there they shall be
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 27:22

phrases.aramaic: עַד יוֹם פׇּקְדִי אוֹתָם נְאֻם ה׳״.
phrases.english: until the day that I remember them, says ה׳."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the source for רב יהודה's ruling, which was stated just before this section.
steps.raayaObject: רב יהודה's ruling that one may not leave בבל for ארץ ישראל.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ירמיהו 27:22: "there they shall be until the day I remember them."

steps.title: רבי זירא: that verse is about the Temple vessels
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא says the פסוק in ירמיהו is about the כלי שרת, not about people.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how does רבי זירא read it? That פסוק is written about the Temple service vessels.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רבי זירא deals with רב יהודה's פסוק. He answers that the פסוק is talking about the Temple vessels being taken to בבל, not about the Jewish people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse just before it speaks about the vessels left in the בית המקדש. So "they shall be brought to Babylonia" means the vessels, and the פסוק says nothing about whether a person may leave בבל. That removes רב יהודה's proof.

keyTerms.meaning: The vessels used for the service in the בית המקדש

phrases.english: And Rabbi Zeira?
That one is written about the service vessels.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי זֵירָא — הָהוּא בִּכְלֵי שָׁרֵת כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from the פסוק in step 1 by reading it as being about something else.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from ירמיהו 27:22 is rejected. רב יהודה's ruling itself is not addressed yet.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק is about the Temple vessels, not about people living in בבל.

steps.title: רב יהודה brings a second verse: the oath in שיר השירים
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה brings the oath "השבעתי אתכם" from שיר השירים as another source.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יהודה? Another פסוק is written: "I make you swear, daughters of Jerusalem, by the gazelles or by the deer of the field..."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רב יהודה answers this. It says he has another source: ה׳'s oath in שיר השירים not to "wake up the love" before its time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if the ירמיהו פסוק is about vessels, רב יהודה reads this oath as telling the Jews not to push the גאולה early. Going up from בבל to ארץ ישראל would count as pushing it, so it is still forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: And so on, meaning the rest of the פסוק

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda?
Another verse is written:
"I make you swear, O daughters of Jerusalem,
phrases.notes: שיר השירים 2:7

phrases.english: by the gazelles or by the deer of the field, etc."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רב יהודה's ruling with a new source after his first one was pushed aside.
steps.raayaObject: רב יהודה's ruling that one may not go up from בבל.

steps.title: רבי זירא: the oath only forbids going up as a mass
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא limits the oath: the nation may not go up all together "like a wall", but individuals may.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי זירא? That oath means the Jews should not go up as a wall.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers רב יהודה's new source. He reads the oath as banning a mass return of the whole nation, not one person moving.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "בחומה" means the nation going up together like a solid wall. Since the oath is only about that, a single person like רבי זירא is not included, so the oath does not stop him.

keyTerms.meaning: That they should not go up
Like a wall, all together as one mass

steps.confusionAlert: רבי זירא is not saying the oath does not exist. He agrees there is an oath; he only limits what it forbids.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Zeira?
That one is so that Israel should not go up as a wall.
phrases.notes: "As a wall" means everyone together in one big group, not one person at a time.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי זֵירָא — הָהוּא שֶׁלֹּא יַעֲלוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּחוֹמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows רב יהודה's second source so it does not apply to an individual.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: It rejects using this oath to forbid an individual from going up.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The oath is about the whole nation going up together, not a single person.

steps.title: רב יהודה: there is another 'I adjure you'
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה points to a second "השבעתי" in שיר השירים for the ban on going up as a wall, which leaves the first one for individuals.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יהודה? Another "I make you swear" is written.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers that the oath appears more than once. One oath covers "not as a wall", and the extra one forbids even individuals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument is based on the repeated phrase. Since the פסוקים in שיר השירים repeat the oath, each one must teach something. For רב יהודה, the extra oath adds the ban on any person going up early.

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda?
Another "I make you swear" is written.
phrases.notes: שיר השירים 3:5

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי זירא's narrowing by pointing to a repeated oath.
steps.terutzResolutionType: An extra פסוק: the repeated oath takes care of "as a wall", so the other oath stays as a ban on individuals.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי זירא thought the oath only covers going up as a wall.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because there is a second oath, רב יהודה uses one for "as a wall" and one for individuals.

steps.title: רבי זירא: the extra oath is needed for the three oaths
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא says the repeated oaths are used up by רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's teaching of three separate oaths: not to go up as a wall, not to rebel against the nations, and for the nations not to oppress Israel too much.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי זירא? He needs that פסוק for the teaching of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא, who said: Why are there these three oaths? One, that Israel should not go up as a wall. One, that ה׳ made Israel swear not to rebel against the nations of the world. And one, that ה׳ made the nations swear not to oppress Israel too much.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers רב יהודה's extra oath. He says each oath in שיר השירים already has its own job, according to רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא, so no oath is left over to forbid individuals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are three oaths, and רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא gives each one a separate meaning. Only one of them is about going up, and it only covers going up "as a wall". So רבי זירא can still allow an individual to go up.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it for something else

steps.whatToRemember: רב יהודה forbids leaving בבל, from ירמיהו and the oaths. רבי זירא pushes each source aside: the ירמיהו פסוק is about the Temple vessels, and the oaths are used up by the three oaths of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא, which only forbid going up "as a wall".
steps.whyThisMatters: The שלש שבועות is a famous teaching: two oaths on Israel, and one on the nations not to oppress Israel too much.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Zeira?
He needs that one
for that of Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina, who said:
Why are there these three oaths?
phrases.notes: The oath appears three times in שיר השירים: 2:7, 3:5, 8:4.

phrases.english: One, that Israel should not go up as a wall,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַחַת שֶׁהִשְׁבִּיעַ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל
phrases.english: and one, that the Holy One, Blessed be He, made Israel swear
that they should not rebel against the nations of the world,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַחַת שֶׁהִשְׁבִּיעַ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אֶת הַגּוֹיִם
phrases.english: and one, that the Holy One, Blessed be He, made the nations swear

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא יִשְׁתַּעְבְּדוּ בָּהֶן בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל יוֹתֵר מִדַּאי.
phrases.english: that they should not oppress Israel too much.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי זֵירָא — הָהוּא מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְכִדְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יהודה's extra oath by showing that each oath is already used for a different lesson.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The extra פסוק is needed for another teaching, so nothing is left over for רב יהודה's ruling.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב יהודה thought the repeated oath was extra and could forbid individuals from going up.
steps.terutzMaskana: All three oaths are used by רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא, and the only one about going up forbids only a mass return "as a wall".

steps.title: רב יהודה finds his source in the doubled phrase
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה answers that the doubled wording "אם תעירו ואם תעוררו" gives him an extra teaching: individuals may not go up either.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יהודה? It is written: "That you not awaken and that you not stir up."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רב יהודה can still hold his view after רבי זירא used up the extra oaths. The answer is that the פסוק repeats itself ("awaken" and "stir up"), and רב יהודה learns his ban on individuals from that repetition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 6, רבי זירא used up the second "השבעתי" for the three oaths of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא. רב יהודה replies that he does not need a second oath at all. The double wording inside the oath itself is enough to add a second ban, so individuals are forbidden too.

keyTerms.meaning: "That you not awaken and that you not stir up" — the doubled wording of the oath

phrases.english: And רב יהודה? [How does he answer this?]
"That you not awaken and that you not stir up" is written.
phrases.notes: שיר השירים 2:7. The פסוק says it twice, and he learns the extra ban on individuals from that.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רב יהודה after רבי זירא used up the repeated oaths in step 6
steps.terutzResolutionType: Finds a new extra word in the פסוק to serve as the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Once the second "השבעתי" is used up, רב יהודה would seem to have no source for banning individuals
steps.terutzMaskana: The doubled verb "תעירו / תעוררו" adds the extra ban on individuals

steps.title: רבי זירא uses the doubled phrase for רבי לוי's six oaths
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא says the doubled phrase is needed for רבי לוי's count of six oaths. Three are the ones already said, and three are new: do not reveal the end, do not push the end away, and do not reveal the secret to the nations.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי זירא? He needs it for the teaching of רבי לוי, who said: Why are there these six oaths? Three are the ones we already said. The other three are: that they not reveal the end, that they not push off the end, and that they not reveal the secret to the nations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what רבי זירא does with the doubled phrase. He answers that it is already used for רבי לוי's teaching, so it cannot be used to ban individuals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי לוי counts six oaths in these פסוקים, and every repeated word is needed to reach that count. Three are the ones from step 6. The other three are about the final redemption: do not reveal when it comes, do not say it is far away, and do not reveal Israel's secret to the nations. Since every repetition is used up, nothing is left over for רב יהודה's ban on individuals, so רבי זירא may go up.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it (for a different teaching)
The end — the time of the final redemption
Push away, make seem far off

steps.whatToRemember: This ends the debate. רב יהודה learns a ban on individuals from the extra wording, while רבי זירא uses all the extra wording for רבי לוי's six oaths, so individuals may go up.

phrases.english: And רבי זירא? [What does he do with this phrase?]
He needs it for the teaching of רבי לוי,
who said: Why are there these six oaths?
Three are the ones we already said,
phrases.notes: These are the three oaths of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא from step 6.

phrases.english: the others are: that they not reveal the end,
and that they not push off the end,
and that they not reveal the secret to the nations.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי זֵירָא מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְכִדְרַבִּי לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers for רבי זירא against רב יהודה's use of the doubled phrase in step 7
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the extra wording is already needed for another teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The doubled phrase seems free to teach a ban on individuals
steps.terutzMaskana: The doubled phrase is used for רבי לוי's six oaths, so it gives no ban on individuals

steps.title: The warning hidden in "gazelles and hinds of the field"
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains that the oath is sworn "by the gazelles and hinds of the field" because if Israel breaks it, their flesh will be left unprotected like wild animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: "By the gazelles or by the hinds of the field." רבי אלעזר said: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Israel: If you keep the oath, good. If not, I will leave your flesh unprotected, like the gazelles and the hinds of the field.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains another phrase in the same oath פסוק. רבי אלעזר says it is a warning about what happens if the oath is broken.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Gazelles and hinds are wild animals that anyone may hunt, and nobody protects them. רבי אלעזר reads the phrase as a threat: if Israel breaks the oaths, ה׳ will remove His protection and they will be open to attack. This shows how serious the oaths are.

phrases.english: "By the gazelles or by the hinds of the field"
phrases.notes: שיר השירים 2:7 — the same oath פסוק.

phrases.english: רבי אלעזר said:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶם הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְיִשְׂרָאֵל,
phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Israel:

phrases.aramaic: אִם אַתֶּם מְקַיְּימִין אֶת הַשְּׁבוּעָה — מוּטָב,
phrases.english: If you keep the oath, good,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם לָאו — אֲנִי מַתִּיר אֶת בְּשַׂרְכֶם
phrases.english: and if not, I will leave your flesh unprotected
like the gazelles and like the hinds of the field.
phrases.notes: These are wild animals that anyone is allowed to hunt, so nobody protects them.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּצְבָאוֹת אוֹ בְּאַיְלוֹת הַשָּׂדֶה אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from counting the oaths to explaining another phrase in the same פסוק
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Breaking the oaths removes ה׳'s protection, leaving Israel unprotected like wild animals

steps.title: Living in ארץ ישראל brings forgiveness
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר teaches that whoever lives in ארץ ישראל lives without sin, and he brings a פסוק from ישעיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: Anyone who lives in ארץ ישראל lives without sin, as it says: "And the inhabitant shall not say: I am sick; the people that dwell in it are forgiven sin."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching of רבי אלעזר, this time about how great it is to live in ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר reads the end of the פסוק, "the people that dwell in it are forgiven sin", as a promise to everyone who lives in the land. He sees living in ארץ ישראל itself as a cause of forgiveness.

keyTerms.meaning: Forgiven of sin (literally: sin is carried away)

phrases.english: רבי אלעזר said:
Anyone who lives in ארץ ישראל
lives without sin,
as it says: "And the inhabitant shall not say: I am sick;"
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 33:24

phrases.english: "the people that dwell in it are forgiven sin."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר כׇּל הַדָּר בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching from the same רבי אלעזר, now about the greatness of ארץ ישראל
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Living in ארץ ישראל brings forgiveness of sin

steps.title: רבא limits the promise to people who suffer illness
steps.stepSummary: רבא tells רב אשי that they learn this פסוק as talking about people who suffer illness, so the forgiveness comes to them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to רב אשי: We learn it as being about those who suffer illnesses.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a narrower reading of רבי אלעזר's פסוק. In his reading, the forgiveness belongs to those who are sick.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא focuses on the words "I am sick" in the פסוק. He reads it as saying that people who suffer illness are the ones forgiven, so the פסוק does not promise forgiveness to every resident just for living there.

keyTerms.meaning: We learn it / we teach it

phrases.english: רבא said to רב אשי:
We learn it as being about those who suffer illnesses.
phrases.notes: He reads "I am sick" in the פסוק as telling you who gets forgiven: the sick.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי אֲנַן בְּסוֹבְלֵי חֳלָאִים מַתְנֵינַן לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the reading of the פסוק that רבי אלעזר brought in step 10
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Limits the scope of the promise. It does not deny that the פסוק promises forgiveness.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק's words "I am sick" show it is talking about the sick, not every resident

steps.title: Burial in the Land is like burial under the altar
steps.stepSummary: רב ענן teaches that anyone buried in ארץ ישראל is like someone buried under the מזבח. He proves it from the shared word אדמה in two פסוקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ענן said: Anyone buried in ארץ ישראל is as if he is buried under the מזבח. One פסוק says 'An altar of earth (אדמה) you shall make for Me,' and another says 'He atones for His land (אדמתו), His people.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching in praise of ארץ ישראל. Being buried there brings atonement, like the מזבח does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אדמה appears in both פסוקים. In one it is tied to the מזבח, and in the other it is tied to atonement for the people. Linking the two teaches that the earth of ארץ ישראל atones, just like the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: The altar in the בית המקדש, where קרבנות bring atonement
Earth or soil. This is the shared word that links the two פסוקים
'It is written here... and it is written there.' This is how the גמרא links two פסוקים through a shared word

phrases.english: Rav Anan said:
Anyone who is buried in the Land of Israel
is as if he is buried beneath the altar.
It is written here:
"An altar of earth you shall make for Me,"
phrases.notes: שמות 20:21

phrases.english: and it is written there:
"And He atones for His land, His people."
phrases.notes: דברים 32:43. The link is the shared word: אדמה and אדמתו.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another teaching in praise of ארץ ישראל, this time about burial and atonement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Burial in ארץ ישראל brings atonement like burial under the מזבח.

steps.title: עולא dies outside the Land
steps.stepSummary: עולא, who used to travel to ארץ ישראל, died in חוץ לארץ. רבי אלעזר applies to him the פסוק 'on an impure land you shall die.'
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא used to go up to the Land of Israel, but he died outside the Land. They came and told רבי אלעזר. He said: You, עולא, 'on an impure land you shall die.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story. רבי אלעזר mourns that עולא died outside ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר sees dying in חוץ לארץ as a real loss, even for a great חכם who kept visiting ארץ ישראל. This sets up the next exchange about bringing his body back.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'his soul rested.' It is a gentle way of saying he died
Impure land. Here it means land outside ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: Ulla was accustomed
to go up to the Land of Israel,
but he died outside the Land.
They came and told Rabbi Elazar.
He said: You, Ulla,
"on an impure land you shall die."
phrases.notes: עמוס 7:17

steps.triggerLanguage: עוּלָּא הֲוָה רְגִיל דַּהֲוָה סָלֵיק לְאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After praising burial in the Land, the גמרא tells of someone who died outside it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dying outside ארץ ישראל is a loss, as the פסוק describes.

steps.title: But his coffin is being brought to the Land
steps.stepSummary: The people point out that עולא's coffin is being brought to ארץ ישראל for burial. So why mourn?
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: His coffin is coming.
steps.whatsHappening: The people push back on רבי אלעזר's lament. They say עולא will still be buried in ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Based on רב ענן's teaching, burial in the Land brings atonement. So it seems the problem is fixed if the body is brought there.

phrases.english: They said to him: His coffin is coming.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אלעזר's lament from step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's sad reaction to עולא's death
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If he will be buried in the Land anyway, he still gets its benefit, so there seems to be no reason to mourn.

steps.title: Living in the Land is not like being buried there after death
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר answers that the Land taking in a person while he is alive cannot be compared to taking him in only after death.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: The Land taking someone in while he is alive is not like the Land taking him in after death.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר defends his lament. Being brought back after death is much less than living and dying in ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Burial in the Land still has value. But the main greatness is to be 'taken in' by the Land during one's life, and that is what עולא missed.

keyTerms.meaning: 'She absorbs him,' meaning the Land takes him in

steps.whatToRemember: Living in ארץ ישראל is greater than only being buried there. Still, burial there brings atonement.

phrases.english: He said to them:
It is not the same when she takes him in while alive
phrases.notes: 'She' is the Land of Israel.

phrases.english: as when she takes him in after death.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between two levels of connection to the Land
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Burial in the Land fully makes up for dying outside it.
steps.terutzMaskana: Being taken in by the Land while alive is far greater than burial after death.

steps.title: May a man leave the Land to do יבום?
steps.stepSummary: A man's childless brother died, and the widow lives in בי חוזאה in בבל. He asks רבי חנינא whether he may go down there to do יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man had a יבמה fall to him in בי חוזאה. He came before רבי חנינא and asked: May I go down and do יבום with her?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new story. A man asks whether he may leave ארץ ישראל to do the מצוה of יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This tests how strongly the value of living in ארץ ישראל holds. The question is whether it holds even against going abroad to do a מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: A widow whose husband died without children, waiting for the brother-in-law to do יבום
To do יבום, marrying the brother's widow
To go down, meaning to leave ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: A certain man
to whom a yevama fell, in Bei Chozaah,
phrases.notes: 'Fell to him' means he became the one responsible for יבום. בי חוזאה is a far-off area in בבל.

phrases.english: came before Rabbi Chanina,
and said to him: May I go down and do yibum with her?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא גַּבְרָא דִּנְפַלָה לֵיהּ יְבָמָה בֵּי חוֹזָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story on the same theme: leaving ארץ ישראל.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether he may leave ארץ ישראל to do the מצוה of יבום.

steps.title: רבי חנינא says not to follow the brother out
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא says the brother left the Land, married a woman abroad, and died. That was a punishment, so this man should not follow him down.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: His brother married a כותית and died. Blessed is God who killed him. And this man wants to go down after him?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא answers with strong words, telling the man not to leave ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא treats the brother's leaving and marrying abroad as so wrong that his death was a fitting punishment. So the surviving brother should not repeat the same mistake, even for יבום.

keyTerms.meaning: A Kutite woman. Here it is a harsh way of describing a wife from outside ארץ ישראל

steps.confusionAlert: The woman was not really a כותית. רבי חנינא calls her that only to show how bad it was to leave the Land to marry her.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי חנינא discourages leaving ארץ ישראל even to do the מצוה of יבום.

phrases.english: He said to him:
His brother married a Kutite woman and died —
Blessed is the Omnipresent who killed him.
And he should go down after him?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the man's question from step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No. He should not leave ארץ ישראל to follow his brother, even for יבום.

steps.title: Do not leave בבל for other lands
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that leaving בבל for other countries is forbidden, just like leaving ארץ ישראל for בבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: Just as it is forbidden to leave ארץ ישראל for בבל, so too it is forbidden to leave בבל for other lands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new rule from שמואל. It sets up a ladder: ארץ ישראל on top, then בבל, then everywhere else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the topic was leaving ארץ ישראל. שמואל adds a second level: בבל has its own holiness compared to other lands, so leaving it is also forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Babylonia, the great Jewish center outside ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:

phrases.aramaic: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁאָסוּר לָצֵאת מֵאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל לְבָבֶל
phrases.english: Just as it is forbidden to leave Eretz Yisrael for Babylonia,

phrases.aramaic: כָּךְ אָסוּר לָצֵאת מִבָּבֶל לִשְׁאָר אֲרָצוֹת.
phrases.english: so too it is forbidden to leave Babylonia for the other lands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the theme of leaving ארץ ישראל to a parallel rule about leaving בבל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Leaving בבל for other lands is forbidden, just like leaving ארץ ישראל for בבל.

steps.title: Even a short move from פומבדיתא to בי כובי
steps.stepSummary: רבה and רב יוסף say the ban applies even to moving from פומבדיתא to the nearby town of בי כובי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה and רב יוסף both say: Even moving from פומבדיתא to בי כובי is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים widen שמואל's rule. Even a short trip across the border of the בבל heartland counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think the rule is only about moving far away. רבה and רב יוסף teach that the border matters, not the distance: בי כובי is close, but it is outside proper בבל.

keyTerms.meaning: פומבדיתא, a major Torah center in בבל
A nearby town outside proper בבל

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think this is about the distance traveled. בי כובי is close; the problem is that it lies outside the borders of בבל.

phrases.english: Rabba and Rav Yosef both say:
Even from Pumbedita to Bei Kuvei.
phrases.notes: He means it is forbidden even to move there; בי כובי sits just past the edge of בבל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands שמואל's rule to include even a short move out of the בבל heartland.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ban on leaving בבל includes even moving from פומבדיתא to בי כובי.

steps.title: רב יוסף excommunicates a man who moved
steps.stepSummary: A man moved from פומבדיתא to בי כובי, and רב יוסף placed him in שמתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man left פומבדיתא for בי כובי, and רב יוסף excommunicated him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that shows רב יוסף really acted on his ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not just theory. רב יוסף treated the move as serious enough to place the man in שמתא, showing how strictly the rule from the step before was taken.

keyTerms.meaning: He placed him in שמתא (excommunicated him)

phrases.english: A certain man who left Pumbedita for Bei Kuvei,
Rav Yosef excommunicated him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A real case that puts the ruling of רבה and רב יוסף into action.
steps.raayaObject: The ruling that even moving from פומבדיתא to בי כובי is forbidden.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב יוסף's actual practice of excommunicating such a person.

steps.title: A scholar moves to אסתוניא and dies
steps.stepSummary: A man moved from פומבדיתא to אסתוניא and died; אביי says that if he had wanted, he would still be alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man left פומבדיתא for אסתוניא and died. אביי said: If this young Torah scholar had wanted, he would be alive.
steps.whatsHappening: A second story shows the danger of leaving בבל. אביי blames the death on the move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first story showed a punishment from בית דין. This one shows a punishment from heaven: had he stayed in בבל, he would have lived.
steps.whatToRemember: Leaving בבל was treated with real seriousness: one man got שמתא from רב יוסף, and another, according to אביי, lost his life.

phrases.english: A certain man who left Pumbedita for Astonia died.
Abaye said:

phrases.aramaic: אִי בָּעֵי הַאי צוּרְבָּא מֵרַבָּנַן, הֲוָה חָיֵי.
phrases.english: If this young Torah scholar had wanted, he would be alive.
phrases.notes: He means he could have chosen to stay in בבל, and then he would not have died.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second story, this time showing a punishment from heaven for leaving בבל.
steps.raayaObject: The seriousness of the ban on leaving בבל.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The scholar's death after moving to אסתוניא, and אביי's comment about it.

steps.title: ארץ ישראל takes in the worthy of בבל
steps.stepSummary: רבה and רב יוסף say ארץ ישראל 'takes in' the worthy people of בבל, and בבל takes in the worthy people of other lands.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה and רב יוסף both say: The worthy people in בבל, ארץ ישראל takes them in. The worthy people in other lands, בבל takes them in.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement keeps the same ladder: ארץ ישראל, then בבל, then other lands. It does not say in what way they are 'taken in,' and that sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each land 'absorbs' the best people from the level below it. The word קולטתן is unclear, so the גמרא will need to explain what kind of absorbing is meant.

phrases.english: Rabba and Rav Yosef both say:
The worthy of Babylonia, Eretz Yisrael takes them in;
the worthy of the other lands, Babylonia takes them in.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה וְרַב יוֹסֵף דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ: כְּשֵׁרִין שֶׁבְּבָבֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new statement by the same pair of אמוראים, using the same ladder of lands.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ארץ ישראל takes in the worthy of בבל, and בבל takes in the worthy of other lands.

steps.title: In what way are they taken in?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'takes them in' refers to.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what matter?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question: what does 'takes them in' mean here? This sets up the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The statement could be about family lineage or about something else. The גמרא needs to pin down the subject before it can understand the statement.

phrases.english: For what matter?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the statement of רבה and רב יוסף is about.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What area of law or life the word קולטתן refers to.

steps.title: It cannot be about family lineage
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests יוחסין but rejects it, since בבל's lineage is actually purer than ארץ ישראל's.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means lineage, didn't the Master say: All lands are like mixed dough compared to ארץ ישראל, and ארץ ישראל is like mixed dough compared to בבל!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the idea that the statement is about יוחסין and immediately challenges it with a known teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ארץ ישראל 'took in' בבל's families for lineage, that would mean ארץ ישראל's lineage is the standard. But the known teaching says בבל's lineage is the purest, and ארץ ישראל's is 'mixed' next to it. So the lineage reading fails.
steps.confusionAlert: On lineage, the order flips: בבל is on top, above ארץ ישראל. That is exactly why the lineage reading does not work.

phrases.english: If you say for lineage,
but didn't the Master say:
All lands are dough compared to Eretz Yisrael,
phrases.notes: 'Dough' means a mixture; their family lines are less clear than those of ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: and Eretz Yisrael is dough compared to Babylonia!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers one possible answer to 'for what matter' and knocks it down.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of קולטתן as being about יוחסין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A known teaching says בבל's lineage is purer than ארץ ישראל's, so ארץ ישראל cannot be the higher level for lineage.

steps.title: It is about burial
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes the statement is about קבורה: the worthy of בבל are buried in ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is about burial.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the true meaning: 'taking in' refers to burial.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worthy people of בבל merit being brought to ארץ ישראל for burial, and the worthy of other lands are buried in בבל. This avoids the lineage problem completely.
steps.whatToRemember: 'ארץ ישראל takes in the worthy of בבל' means they merit burial there, not that ארץ ישראל has better lineage.

phrases.english: Rather, it is regarding burial.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the lineage reading, the גמרא gives the correct one.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the subject of the statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: קולטתן might mean ארץ ישראל accepts בבל's families as having good lineage.
steps.terutzMaskana: קולטתן refers to burial: the worthy of בבל are buried in ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: Living in בבל is like living in ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה says living in בבל is like living in ארץ ישראל, based on a פסוק in זכריה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: Whoever lives in בבל, it is as if he lives in ארץ ישראל, as it says: 'Ho, ציון, escape, you who dwell with the daughter of בבל.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה gives בבל a very high rank and backs it up with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק calls the people living in בבל by the name 'ציון.' רב יהודה learns from this that living in בבל counts like living in ארץ ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is said (in a פסוק)
ציון, a name for ירושלים and ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַדָּר בְּבָבֶל כְּאִילּוּ דָּר בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל,
phrases.english: Whoever lives in Babylonia, it is as if he lives in Eretz Yisrael,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״הוֹי צִיּוֹן הִמָּלְטִי יוֹשֶׁבֶת בַּת בָּבֶל״.
phrases.english: as it is said: "Ho, Zion, escape, you who dwell with the daughter of Babylon."
phrases.notes: זכריה 2:11. The people in בבל are called 'ציון' here.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: כׇּל הַדָּר בְּבָבֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues praising בבל with a new statement and a פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Living in בבל is considered like living in ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: בבל will be spared חבלי משיח
steps.stepSummary: אביי reports a tradition that בבל will not see the suffering before משיח comes.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: We have a tradition: בבל will not see the birth pangs of משיח.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי adds another praise of בבל, based on a tradition he received.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חבלי משיח are the hard times expected right before משיח arrives. אביי says בבל will be protected from them.

keyTerms.meaning: We hold / we have a tradition

phrases.english: Abaye said: We have a tradition:
Babylonia will not see the birth pangs of the Messiah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another special quality of בבל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בבל will not experience חבלי משיח.

steps.title: The tradition refers to הוצל דבנימין
steps.stepSummary: אביי's tradition is applied specifically to the town הוצל דבנימין, which is called 'the Horn of Salvation.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He applied it to הוצל דבנימין, and they call it 'קרנא דשיזבתא,' the Horn of Salvation.
steps.whatsHappening: The tradition about בבל is narrowed down to one specific town.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not all of בבל is meant, only the town הוצל דבנימין. That is why people gave it the name 'Horn of Salvation': it will be saved from those hard times.

keyTerms.meaning: הוצל of בנימין, a town in בבל

phrases.english: He applied it to Hutzal deVinyamin,
phrases.notes: 'It' is אביי's tradition from the step before; it is now limited to this one town.

phrases.english: and they call it the Horn of Salvation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows אביי's general tradition about בבל to one town.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The protection from חבלי משיח applies to הוצל דבנימין.

steps.title: The dead outside ארץ ישראל will not come back to life
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר learns from a פסוק in יחזקאל that only the dead of ארץ ישראל will come back to life.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: The dead outside ארץ ישראל will not live again, as it says: 'And I will set glory in the land of the living.' A land that has My desire, its dead will live. A land that does not have My desire, its dead will not live.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a strong statement about תחיית המתים, returning to the special power of ארץ ישראל itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר reads the word צבי in the פסוק like צביוני, 'My desire.' The land God desires is ארץ ישראל, and the פסוק calls it 'the land of the living.' So only its dead will live again.

keyTerms.meaning: Glory; read here as connected to 'desire'

steps.whyThisMatters: This sharp statement sets up the rest of the sugya. It explains the deep wish to live in, or at least be buried in, ארץ ישראל, and it raises an obvious question about the righteous buried outside the Land.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
The dead outside the Land will not live again,
as it is said: "And I will set glory in the land of the living" —
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 26:20

phrases.english: a land that has My desire in it, its dead will live;
phrases.notes: He reads צבי like צביוני, 'My desire,' meaning the land God wants: ארץ ישראל.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין צִבְיוֹנִי בָּהּ — אֵין מֵתֶיהָ חַיִּים.
phrases.english: one that does not have My desire in it, its dead will not live.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: מֵתִים שֶׁבְּחוּץ לָאָרֶץ אֵינָם חַיִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the praise of בבל to the unique power of ארץ ישראל, now about תחיית המתים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dead outside ארץ ישראל will not come back to life, learned from 'ונתתי צבי בארץ חיים.'

steps.title: A verse that seems to say the dead outside the Land also rise
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא בר ממל challenges רבי אלעזר from ישעיהו: 'Your dead shall live' means the dead of ארץ ישראל, and 'my dead bodies shall arise' means the dead of חוץ לארץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא בר ממל objected: 'Your dead shall live; my dead bodies shall arise.' Doesn't 'Your dead shall live' mean the dead in ארץ ישראל, and 'my dead bodies shall arise' mean the dead outside the Land?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא בר ממל attacks רבי אלעזר's claim from step 29 with a פסוק that seems to promise that the dead outside ארץ ישראל will also rise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק has two halves, and he reads each half as a different group of dead people. If the second half is about the dead of חוץ לארץ, then רבי אלעזר's rule that only the dead of ארץ ישראל rise is contradicted.

keyTerms.meaning: is it not that...? (introduces a proposed reading)

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba bar Memel raised an objection:
"Your dead shall live; my dead bodies shall arise"
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 26:19

phrases.english: Is it not that "Your dead shall live"
means the dead in Eretz Yisrael,
and "my dead bodies shall arise"
means the dead outside the Land?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly challenges רבי אלעזר's statement in step 29.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's rule that only the dead of ארץ ישראל will come back to life.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The second half of the פסוק in ישעיהו seems to promise תחיית המתים to the dead of חוץ לארץ as well.

steps.title: Reading רבי אלעזר's verse as being about נבוכדנצר
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא בר ממל removes רבי אלעזר's proof. He says 'ונתתי צבי בארץ חיים' refers to נבוכדנצר, a king as swift as a deer (צבי).
steps.simpleTranslation: And what does 'And I will set צבי in the land of the living' mean? It is written about נבוכדנצר, as the Merciful One says: I will bring upon them a king who is as swift as a deer.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא בר ממל goes on to take away רבי אלעזר's source by giving the word צבי a different meaning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר read 'the land of the living' as the place whose dead will live again. רבי אבא בר ממל reads צבי as 'deer', a picture of the swift king נבוכדנצר. Read that way, the פסוק says nothing about תחיית המתים.

phrases.english: And what is "And I will set glory in the land of the living"?
phrases.notes: This is the יחזקאל פסוק רבי אלעזר used in step 29. The word צבי can mean 'glory' or 'deer'.

phrases.english: It is written about Nebuchadnezzar,
as the Merciful One says:
I will bring upon them a king
who is as swift as a deer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי אבא בר ממל's challenge by neutralizing רבי אלעזר's proof-text.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from יחזקאל, not the idea of ארץ ישראל's special status in general.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The word צבי can be read as 'deer', describing נבוכדנצר, so the פסוק is not about תחיית המתים.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר learns from a different verse
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר answers that his source is really a פסוק in ישעיהו: 'He gives breath to the people upon it, and spirit to those who walk on it.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: My teacher, I expound a different verse: 'He gives breath to the people upon it and spirit to those who walk on it.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר does not argue about the word צבי. Instead, he gives a different פסוק as his real source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says ה׳ gives נשמה to the people who are 'upon it', meaning upon the Land. That suggests new life is given to those of ארץ ישראל. So רבי אלעזר's rule stands even without the verse from יחזקאל.

keyTerms.meaning: expound, learn out from a פסוק

phrases.english: He said to him: My teacher,
I expound a different verse:
"He gives breath to the people upon it
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 42:5

phrases.english: and spirit to those who walk on it."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי מִקְרָא אַחֵר אֲנִי דּוֹרֵשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the דחיה of step 31 by switching to a new source.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replacement source: a different פסוק supports the same rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed that רבי אלעזר's rule depended on the יחזקאל verse, which was just reinterpreted.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אלעזר's rule rests on ישעיהו 42:5, 'the people upon it.'

steps.title: But what about 'my dead bodies shall arise'?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא בר ממל presses again: how does רבי אלעזר explain 'נבלתי יקומון', which seemed to refer to the dead of חוץ לארץ?
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it written: 'My dead bodies shall arise'!
steps.whatsHappening: The challenge from step 30 comes back. Even with a new source, רבי אלעזר still has to explain the פסוק that seemed to include the dead outside the Land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Finding a new proof does not solve the original problem. 'נבלתי יקומון' still seems to say a second group of dead will rise, and that group looked like the dead of חוץ לארץ.

phrases.english: But isn't it written
"My dead bodies shall arise"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the original challenge of step 30 after רבי אלעזר's new source.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's position, even with its new source.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק 'נבלתי יקומון' still seems to promise that a second group of dead, those of חוץ לארץ, will rise.

steps.title: That verse is about stillborns
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains that 'נבלתי יקומון' refers to נפלים (stillborns), not to the dead of חוץ לארץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: That verse is written about stillborns.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers the challenge by saying the second half of the פסוק is about a different group entirely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second group in the פסוק is still a separate group of dead who will rise. But it is נפלים, not people buried outside ארץ ישראל. So the פסוק no longer contradicts רבי אלעזר.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר: only the dead of ארץ ישראל rise (source: 'the people upon it'). 'נבלתי יקומון' is about stillborns. רבי אבא בר ממל: 'נבלתי יקומון' is about the dead of חוץ לארץ, who also rise.

phrases.english: That one is written about stillborns.
phrases.notes: So even babies born dead will come back to life.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 33.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'נבלתי יקומון' refers to the dead of חוץ לארץ.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'נבלתי יקומון' refers to stillborns, so it does not include the dead of חוץ לארץ.

steps.title: How does רבי אבא בר ממל use רבי אלעזר's verse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי אבא בר ממל learns from 'נותן נשמה לעם עליה', since he does not learn רבי אלעזר's rule from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אבא בר ממל, what does he do with this verse 'He gives breath to the people upon it'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next move. It asks what the other side does with this פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פסוק is assumed to teach something. If רבי אבא בר ממל does not use it to limit תחיית המתים to ארץ ישראל, the גמרא wants to know what he learns from it instead.

keyTerms.meaning: what does he do with it? (how does he use this source)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Abba bar Memel,
this verse "He gives breath to the people upon it"
what does he do with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר מֶמֶל הַאי נוֹתֵן נְשָׁמָה לָעָם עָלֶיהָ מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from רבי אלעזר's defense to how the other side reads רבי אלעזר's source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבי אבא בר ממל learns from 'נותן נשמה לעם עליה'.

steps.title: Even a Canaanite maidservant in ארץ ישראל has a share in עולם הבא
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא בר ממל uses the פסוק for רבי אבהו's teaching: even a שפחה כנענית in ארץ ישראל is promised עולם הבא. This is learned by comparing 'לעם' with 'עם החמור'.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs it for the teaching of רבי אבהו, who said: Even a שפחה כנענית in ארץ ישראל is promised a share in עולם הבא. It is written here 'to the people upon it', and it is written there 'Stay here with the donkey', meaning a people that is like a donkey.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי אבא בר ממל uses the פסוק to teach a different lesson about ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word עַם ('people') in our פסוק is linked to עִם ('with') in 'שבו לכם פה עם החמור'. There, the word is read as describing a people compared to a donkey, meaning servants. So 'the people upon it' includes even a שפחה כנענית living in ארץ ישראל, and she receives נשמה in עולם הבא.

keyTerms.meaning: he needs it (for a different teaching)
it says here, and it says there (a word-link between two פסוקים)

phrases.english: He needs it for the teaching of Rabbi Abbahu.
For Rabbi Abbahu said:
Even a Canaanite maidservant
who is in Eretz Yisrael

phrases.aramaic: מוּבְטָח לָהּ שֶׁהִיא בַּת הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא.
phrases.english: is promised that she has a share in the World to Come.
It is written here: "to the people upon it,"
and it is written there:
"Stay here with the donkey"
phrases.notes: בראשית 22:5

phrases.english: meaning a people that is like a donkey.
phrases.notes: The word עִם ('with') is read as עַם ('people'). That links it to לָעָם in our פסוק.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה of step 35.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He uses 'לעם עליה' for רבי אבהו's teaching that even a שפחה כנענית in ארץ ישראל is promised עולם הבא.

steps.title: Walking four אמות in ארץ ישראל earns עולם הבא
steps.stepSummary: On the second half of the פסוק, 'and spirit to those who walk on it', רבי ירמיה בר אבא quotes רבי יוחנן: anyone who walks four אמות in ארץ ישראל is promised a share in עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And spirit to those who walk on it': רבי ירמיה בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Anyone who walks four אמות in ארץ ישראל is promised a share in עולם הבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching built on the second half of the same פסוק from ישעיהו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Those who walk on it' is read as anyone who walks even a short distance in ארץ ישראל. Like the first half of the פסוק, this half also promises life in עולם הבא, tied to the Land.

keyTerms.meaning: one who has a share in the World to Come

steps.whatToRemember: Both halves of ישעיהו 42:5 praise ארץ ישראל. 'The people upon it' teaches that even a שפחה כנענית there has עולם הבא. 'Those who walk on it' teaches that walking four אמות there earns עולם הבא.

phrases.english: "And spirit to those who walk on it":
Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
Anyone who walks four amos
in Eretz Yisrael

phrases.aramaic: מוּבְטָח לוֹ שֶׁהוּא בֶּן הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא.
phrases.english: is promised that he has a share in the World to Come.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרוּחַ לַהוֹלְכִים בָּהּ אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second half of the same פסוק whose first half was used in step 36.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Anyone who walks four אמות in ארץ ישראל is promised a share in עולם הבא.

steps.title: What about the righteous who die outside the Land?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אלעזר: does his view mean that the righteous buried outside ארץ ישראל will never come alive at תחיית המתים?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי אלעזר, the righteous people outside ארץ ישראל will not come alive?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי אלעזר's rule that the dead outside ארץ ישראל will not come alive. It sounds impossible that even righteous people would lose תחיית המתים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר's rule seemed to cover everyone buried outside the Land. The challenge is that righteous people surely deserve to be brought back to life, so the rule cannot be that simple.

keyTerms.meaning: The time when the dead come back to life

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Elazar,
the righteous outside the Land will not come alive?!
phrases.notes: This means at the time the dead come back to life.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר, צַדִּיקִים שֶׁבְּחוּץ לָאָרֶץ אֵינָם חַיִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רבי אלעזר's rule and challenges its result for the righteous.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's view that the dead outside ארץ ישראל do not come alive
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It cannot be that righteous people lose תחיית המתים just because of where they are buried.

steps.title: They will roll to the Land
steps.stepSummary: רבי אילעא answers that the righteous outside the Land will roll through the ground to ארץ ישראל and come alive there.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אילעא said: They will come alive by means of rolling.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אילעא defends רבי אלעזר. The righteous will come alive, but only after rolling to ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This keeps רבי אלעזר's rule that coming back to life happens in ארץ ישראל. The righteous are not left out. They are simply moved to the Land first.

keyTerms.meaning: Rolling (moving through the ground to ארץ ישראל)

phrases.english: Rabbi Ile'a said:
By means of rolling.
phrases.notes: He means their bodies will roll underground until they reach ארץ ישראל.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אִילְעָא: עַל יְדֵי גִּלְגּוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 38.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains how the righteous come alive without breaking רבי אלעזר's rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The righteous outside the Land would never come alive.
steps.terutzMaskana: They come alive after rolling to ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: Rolling would be painful
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא סלא רבא objects that rolling through the ground is suffering, and the righteous should not have to suffer.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא סלא רבא strongly objected: Rolling is suffering for the righteous!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא סלא רבא attacks רבי אילעא's answer. Rolling through the earth would cause pain, which does not fit how the righteous should be treated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem is no longer whether the righteous come alive, but how. An answer that makes the righteous suffer is hard to accept.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַבִּי אַבָּא סַלָּא רַבָּא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba Salla Rava strongly objected to this:
Rolling is suffering for the righteous!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַבִּי אַבָּא סַלָּא רַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in Step 39.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Rolling causes pain, and the righteous should not be made to suffer.

steps.title: Tunnels are made for them
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that tunnels are made in the ground for the righteous, so they can travel to ארץ ישראל without suffering.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Tunnels are made for them in the ground.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי fixes the problem of pain. The righteous travel through ready-made tunnels instead of rolling through solid earth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea of moving to ארץ ישראל stays in place. Only the way they travel changes, so the righteous do not suffer.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אלעזר, the righteous outside ארץ ישראל still come alive. They reach the Land through tunnels that are made for them.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Tunnels are made for them in the ground.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: מְחִילּוֹת נַעֲשׂוֹת לָהֶם בַּקַּרְקַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of Step 40.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changes the way they travel so there is no suffering
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The righteous would have to roll painfully through the earth.
steps.terutzMaskana: Tunnels are prepared, so they reach ארץ ישראל without pain.

steps.title: Why יעקב wanted to be buried in the Land
steps.stepSummary: קרנא explains that יעקב asked to be carried out of מצרים because, even though he was fully righteous, he feared he might not merit the tunnels.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Carry me out of מצרים and bury me in their burial place.' קרנא said: There is a hidden meaning here. יעקב knew he was fully righteous. If the dead outside the Land come alive, why did he trouble his sons? Because he feared he might not merit the tunnels.
steps.whatsHappening: קרנא uses the idea of the tunnels to explain a פסוק about יעקב. He asks why יעקב troubled his sons to bury him in ארץ ישראל, and answers with the fear of not meriting the tunnels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the righteous can reach the Land through tunnels, יעקב did not seem to need burial there. The answer is that he was not sure he would merit the tunnels, so being buried in the Land was the safer way.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a hidden meaning inside

phrases.english: "You shall carry me out of Egypt
phrases.notes: בראשית מז:ל

phrases.english: and bury me in their burial place,"
Karna said: There are matters inside it:
Our forefather Jacob knew
that he was completely righteous,
and if the dead outside the Land come alive,
why did he trouble his sons?
Lest he not merit the tunnels.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on אביי's tunnels to explain a פסוק about יעקב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יעקב insisted on burial in ארץ ישראל because he was afraid he might not merit the tunnels.

steps.title: The same idea about יוסף
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא gives the same explanation for יוסף's oath. יוסף made his brothers carry his bones four hundred פרסאות because he feared he might not merit the tunnels.
steps.simpleTranslation: Similarly you say: 'And יוסף made the children of Israel swear.' רבי חנינא said: There is a hidden meaning here. יוסף knew he was fully righteous. If the dead outside the Land come alive, why did he trouble his brothers four hundred פרסאות? Because he feared he might not merit the tunnels.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a matching teaching about יוסף. It follows the same pattern as the one about יעקב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יוסף's case is even stronger, because carrying his bones meant a journey of four hundred פרסאות. Even so, he chose that heavy burden over the risk of not meriting the tunnels.

phrases.english: Similarly you say:
"And Joseph made the children of Israel swear, etc."
phrases.notes: בראשית נ:כה

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina said: There are matters inside it:
Joseph knew about himself
that he was completely righteous,
and if the dead outside the Land come alive,
why did he trouble his brothers
four hundred parasangs?
Lest he not merit the tunnels.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a matching teaching about יוסף, parallel to יעקב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יוסף demanded that his bones be brought to ארץ ישראל because he feared he might not merit the tunnels.

steps.title: A letter to רבה repeats the teaching
steps.stepSummary: רבה's brothers in ארץ ישראל send him a letter in בבל containing the teaching that יעקב knew he was fully righteous.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה's brothers sent him: 'יעקב knew that he was completely righteous, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports that this teaching was sent in a letter to רבה. This line sets up the next step, where אילפא adds a story to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The teaching about יעקב is repeated here because it was being sent to רבה, who lived outside the Land. It serves as the base for the story that comes next.

phrases.english: Rabbah's brothers sent to him:

phrases.aramaic: יוֹדֵעַ הָיָה יַעֲקֹב שֶׁצַּדִּיק גָּמוּר הָיָה וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: Jacob knew that he was completely righteous, etc.
phrases.notes: "Etc." means the rest of קרנא's teaching from Step 42.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the יעקב teaching as part of a letter, setting up אילפא's addition.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The teaching about יעקב's burial was sent to רבה in בבל.

steps.title: The man who would not leave the Land
steps.stepSummary: אילפא adds a story about a man who wanted to leave ארץ ישראל because of a woman he longed for. After hearing this teaching, he stayed and suffered until the day he died.
steps.simpleTranslation: אילפא adds to it: There was a man who was suffering over a certain woman and wanted to leave the Land. When he heard this teaching, he endured his suffering until the day he died.
steps.whatsHappening: אילפא tells a story showing how strongly this teaching affected people. A man gave up leaving the Land, even though staying meant living with his pain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The teaching about יעקב shows how important it is to be in ארץ ישראל. The story turns that idea into real life: the man chose a lifetime of suffering over leaving the Land.

keyTerms.meaning: To go down (to leave ארץ ישראל)

steps.whatToRemember: The righteous outside the Land come alive through tunnels. Still, יעקב and יוסף insisted on burial in ארץ ישראל, and people were willing to suffer rather than leave it.

phrases.english: Ilfa adds matters to it:
There was an incident with one who was suffering
over a certain woman,
and he wanted to go down,
once he heard this,
he endured his suffering until the day of his death.
phrases.notes: Literally "he rolled himself." It means he lived with his pain and stayed in the Land.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a story to the teaching quoted in the letter.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hearing how much יעקב valued burial in ארץ ישראל, a man chose to suffer for the rest of his life rather than leave the Land.

steps.title: Learning from a teacher beats learning alone
steps.stepSummary: The letter urges רבה to come to ארץ ישראל. Even a great חכם gains more from a teacher, and רבי יוחנן is there to teach him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even though you are a great sage, someone who learns by himself is not like someone who learns from his teacher. And if you say you have no teacher here, you do have one. Who is he? רבי יוחנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The letter from רבה's brothers continues. They give him a reason to move to ארץ ישראל: learning from a רב is better than learning alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They expect רבה to answer, 'I am already a great חכם, so I don't need a teacher.' They answer that no matter how great you are, a teacher adds something. They also block the excuse that there is no one worthy to teach him by naming רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: one who learns from his teacher

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a well-known source that even a great scholar gains from having a רב to learn from.

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁחָכָם גָּדוֹל אַתָּה,
phrases.english: Even though you are a great sage,
phrases.notes: This is still the letter רבה's brothers sent him, talking straight to him.

phrases.english: one who learns by himself is not comparable
to one who learns from his teacher.
And if you say you have no teacher here,

phrases.aramaic: יֵשׁ לְךָ רַב, וּמַנּוּ — רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן.
phrases.english: you do have a teacher. And who is he? רבי יוחנן.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁחָכָם גָּדוֹל אַתָּה

steps.title: Health advice: split time between sitting, standing and walking
steps.stepSummary: If רבה will not come up, he should be careful in three things. Too much sitting, standing or walking each causes harm, so he should spend a third of his time on each.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you do not come up, be careful about three things. Do not sit too much, because sitting is bad for hemorrhoids. Do not stand too much, because standing is bad for the heart. Do not walk too much, because walking is bad for the eyes. Instead: one third sitting, one third standing, one third walking.
steps.whatsHappening: The brothers give רבה a back-up plan in case he stays in בבל. They give him practical health advice about balancing his daily activities.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each activity has its own harm when overdone: sitting affects the lower body, standing the heart, and walking the eyes. The solution is balance, an equal third of the time for each.

phrases.english: And if you do not come up,
be careful in three things:
Do not sit too much,
because sitting is harmful for hemorrhoids,
and do not stand too much,
because standing is harmful to the heart,
and do not walk too much,
because walking is harmful to the eyes.
Rather, one third sitting,
one third standing, one third walking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After urging him to come, the letter gives advice for the case where רבה stays in בבל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Too much sitting, standing or walking each causes harm, so a person should spend one third of his time on each.

steps.title: Sitting without support is worse than standing
steps.stepSummary: The letter adds that standing is more comfortable than sitting when there is nothing to lean on.
steps.simpleTranslation: Any sitting without something to lean on: standing is more comfortable than that.
steps.whatsHappening: The letter gives another piece of health advice about sitting. Sitting with no back support is less comfortable than standing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds a detail to the sitting rule: sitting is only restful when you have support. This line sets up the גמרא's challenge in the next step, because it seems to praise standing.

phrases.english: Any sitting that has no support with it,
standing is more comfortable than it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another detail of health advice to the letter.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sitting without support is less comfortable than standing.

steps.title: But standing was just called harmful to the heart
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how standing can be called better, when the letter itself said standing is harmful to the heart.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really think standing is better? But you said standing is harmful to the heart!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the line it just quoted. It points out that it contradicts the letter's earlier warning about standing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 47 said standing is harmful to the heart. Step 48 seems to say standing is better than a kind of sitting. Both lines come from the same letter, so they seem to contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: can it enter your mind? (would you really think so?)

phrases.english: Standing? Can that enter your mind?
But you said standing is harmful to the heart!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of step 48 from the earlier warning in step 47.
steps.kashyaTarget: The statement that standing is more comfortable than sitting without support.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Internal contradiction: the same letter already said standing is harmful to the heart, so it cannot praise standing.

steps.title: Beginning to correct the wording
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts to fix the line by saying 'Rather: sitting…'. The rest of the answer continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: sitting…
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer by restating the line in a new way. This is only the opening word, so it sets up the answer that continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אֶלָּא signals that the earlier wording is being replaced. The new version will be built around sitting, not standing, so that it no longer clashes with the warning that standing hurts the heart.

phrases.english: Rather: sitting
phrases.notes: The answer isn't finished yet; it continues in the next part of the daf.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the contradiction raised in step 49.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rewording the statement (the answer continues on the next amud).

steps.terutzMaskana: The line will be reworded to talk about sitting, so it no longer praises standing. The full wording comes next.
